stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Historians long credited John Kay's flying shuttle, patented in 1733, with doubling a weaver's daily output. The claim seems to follow from the device itself: by letting a single weaver send the shuttle across a broad loom, it eliminated the second worker that such looms had required. ______ many weavers who adopted the shuttle saw little change in how much cloth they finished, since local spinners could not produce yarn quickly enough to keep the faster looms supplied.
explanation: The first two sentences set up an expectation. Historians believed the shuttle doubled output, and the way the device worked makes that belief seem reasonable. The sentence after the blank reports what actually happened: many weavers saw little change. That is not what the first two sentences would lead you to expect, so you need a word that concedes the point and then turns against it. 'Still' means 'even so,' which is exactly that relationship. The 'since' clause gives a reason for the disappointing result. That reason comes from inside the third sentence, not from the sentences before it, so the transition itself must not claim a cause.

A.why: You probably saw the cause words ('since,' 'eliminated') and the shared topic and assumed the sentences run in the same direction. 'For this reason' would mean the device's design caused weavers to see little change. In fact, the design is what made people expect big gains. The real cause, the yarn shortage, is stated after the blank, not before it.

B.why: You correctly saw that the logic turns, but you picked the wrong kind of turn. 'Conversely' introduces the reverse of a relationship already stated, such as 'A raises B; conversely, lowering A lowers B.' This sentence doesn't reverse anything. It admits that a reasonable expectation failed in practice. That calls for a concession like 'still,' not a mirror-image contrast.

D.why: The sentence after the blank narrows to a particular group, the weavers who adopted the shuttle, so it looks like a zoom-in. But 'specifically' introduces a more precise version of the same claim. Here the sentence doesn't restate the claim that output doubled. It contradicts it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over five decades, printmaker Ilse Varga worked in three media and earned recognition in all of them. Her etchings won two international prizes, and her lithographs entered the collections of four national museums. Her woodcuts drew favorable notices at a regional exhibition. ______ it was the woodcuts, the least honored of the three, that Varga called her only serious work, dismissing the rest as "commissions I happened to be good at."
explanation: The first sentences list Varga's honors in three media, and the honors grow smaller toward the end. A reader would expect her to value the most decorated work most, or at least to value all three. The sentence after the blank does the opposite: it ranks the least honored medium above the rest and dismisses the prize-winning work. Because that runs against what the list sets up, you need a concession. 'Even so' means 'despite all that recognition,' which is the relationship here.

A.why: The first sentence names a group, three media, and the sentence after the blank picks out one of them, the woodcuts. That pattern looks like an example. But the sentence doesn't illustrate the claim that she earned recognition in all of them. It reports how Varga herself rejected that recognition. Naming one member of a group is not enough to make an example. The sentence also has to support the claim the group belongs to.

C.why: 'Accordingly' would mean her preference for the woodcuts followed from the honors just listed. It didn't. The honors pointed toward the etchings and lithographs. You checked that both sentences are about the same topic, her work and its reception, but you didn't check which way the logic runs.

D.why: This is the list trap. The passage is a string of achievements, so 'moreover' feels like it adds one more. But the sentence after the blank doesn't add a success. It ranks one medium above all the others and dismisses the rest, which turns against the list. Try putting 'and also' between the sentences: 'and also she dismissed her prize-winning work' sounds wrong, so an addition word can't be right.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many coaches believe that static stretching before a sprint loosens the muscles and so makes athletes faster. In a recent trial with forty collegiate sprinters, the first half of that belief held up: after holding stretches for ninety seconds, the athletes rated their legs as markedly looser than on days when they skipped stretching. ______ their times over 60 meters were, on average, a few hundredths of a second slower on the days they stretched.
explanation: The coaches' belief has two parts: stretching loosens muscles, and looser muscles mean more speed. The sentence before the blank confirms only the first part. The sentence after reports the opposite of what that would lead you to expect, because the athletes felt looser and ran slower. You need a word that sets a result against what the previous sentence led you to expect, and 'Even so' does exactly that.

A.why: You saw that both sentences are about the same stretching days and assumed the second follows from the first. Feeling looser did not cause slower times. The slower times are the surprise, and 'For this reason' claims a cause the passage never gives.

B.why: You correctly saw that you needed a concession word, then chose one that belongs in the wrong spot. 'Granted' concedes a point that a later 'but' will push back on. Here the sentence after the blank is already the pushback, and no reversal follows it.

D.why: You read 'the first half of that belief held up' and expected more confirmation. 'Likewise' says the next finding points the same way, but slower times work against the belief instead of supporting it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Engineers designing a lighter bicycle frame hoped that packing more ceramic particles into an aluminum alloy would keep making it stronger. Early results were encouraging: at every concentration from 5 to 15 percent by volume, the reinforced alloy was both stiffer and stronger than plain aluminum. ______ at 20 percent, the reinforced alloy proved weaker than the plain metal, because the particles clumped together and cracks began at the clumps.
explanation: The engineers hoped that more particles would always mean more strength, and the 5-15 percent results supported that hope. At 20 percent the alloy became weaker than plain aluminum, which reverses the pattern. 'Yet' marks that reversal.

A.why: You treated '20 percent' as a closer look at the range you had just read. That range ended at 15 percent, and the new sentence reports a different result. 'Specifically' only restates the previous claim more precisely.

B.why: Both sentences report test results at a given concentration, so you assumed they point the same way. The first reports gains and the second reports a loss, so 'Similarly' sends the logic in the wrong direction.

C.why: The passage explains a mechanism (clumping, then cracking), so you reached for a cause word. That cause sits inside the second sentence. The encouraging results before the blank did not produce the weakness.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Fossil plants have proved useful to scientists in many ways: they let researchers map vanished forests, date layers of volcanic ash, and trace how early farming spread across Europe. ______ the most consequential use of the fossil plant record may be one its first collectors never imagined: estimating past levels of atmospheric carbon dioxide from the density of tiny breathing pores, called stomata, on fossil leaves.
explanation: The first sentence lists several respected uses. The second ranks a different use above all of them, one nobody expected, so it pivots against the list instead of adding to it. 'Still' marks that turn: despite all those uses, the most important one lies elsewhere.

A.why: You saw 'many ways' and expected the next sentence to give one of them. The carbon dioxide use is not one of the listed uses. It is ranked above them and described as unforeseen, so it is not a sample drawn from that group.

C.why: You assumed that a long list of uses leads to the conclusion that follows. Nothing in the list causes the stomata method to be the most important one. 'Accordingly' invents a cause.

D.why: This is the list trap. Both sentences are about uses of fossils, so you read the second as one more item. Because it ranks a never-imagined use above all the others, the second sentence turns against the list, which 'Similarly' cannot express.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Because school handwashing campaigns target the germs that spread through shared food and surfaces, many health officials assume their main payoff is fewer cases of stomach illness. ______ when researchers tracked absences in 60 elementary schools for two years, absences from stomach illness fell only slightly; the much larger drop, nearly a third, came from colds and flu.
explanation: The first sentence gives an assumption, and the second gives the measured reality that corrects it. When a mistaken belief is followed by the true finding, 'In fact' is the natural correction word.

B.why: You saw that a correction was coming and chose a concession word, but 'Admittedly' introduces a point the writer grants before arguing against it. The study finding is the writer's main point, not something conceded.

C.why: The 'Because' in the first sentence pulled you toward a cause word. The officials' assumption did not cause the study's results, and the results contradict the assumption.

D.why: A study with specific numbers looks like an illustration, so you chose an example word. The study does not illustrate the officials' assumption. It overturns it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The linguist who first documented the language in the 1970s recommended writing it in the Latin alphabet, arguing that its sounds mapped neatly onto Spanish spelling. ______ the community's own writing committee, meeting a decade later, adopted a syllabary devised by a local schoolteacher, judging that it captured distinctions in vowel length that Spanish letters ignored.
explanation: The first sentence gives one person's recommendation, and the second reports that the community chose something else. Advice followed by a different choice is a contrast, and 'However' marks it.

A.why: You assumed the committee acted on the linguist's advice because the sentences come one after the other. The committee rejected the Latin alphabet, so 'Accordingly' says the opposite of what happened.

B.why: You may have grouped 'Of course' with the concession words, but it signals that what follows was obvious or expected. The committee's choice went against the expert's advice, so it was not the expected outcome.

D.why: 'Namely' restates the previous idea more precisely. The syllabary is not a sharper version of the linguist's recommendation. It replaces that recommendation.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A vaccine is tested in three stages: first for safety in a few dozen volunteers, then for immune response in a few hundred, and lastly for protection in thousands. A nasal flu vaccine developed in 2021 cleared the first two stages easily, producing antibody levels higher than those of any injected vaccine it was compared with. ______ in the final stage, it protected volunteers no better than a placebo did.
explanation: Record antibody levels lead you to expect strong protection. The final stage showed no protection at all. 'Nonetheless' marks a result that comes despite what came before.

A.why: Nothing about strong early results predicts failure. 'Predictably' calls the outcome expected when the passage presents it as a reversal.

C.why: The three-stage frame primed you for a sequence word, and 'Finally' fits the order of stages. It only marks the next step, though, and misses that the result goes against the first two stages.

D.why: You linked the high antibody levels to the final result as if one produced the other. 'Therefore' claims the early success caused the failure, and the passage makes no such link.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The nineteenth-century luthier Ilse Varga built more than four hundred violins, trained a generation of apprentices across Central Europe, and wrote a treatise on varnish that restorers still consult. ______ the achievement she herself ranked highest was a modest one: a set of graded finger exercises that let village schoolchildren begin string lessons without a private teacher.
explanation: The first sentence lists grand achievements. The second says Varga valued a modest piece of work above all of them, which turns against the list. 'That said' marks that turn.

A.why: The list of achievements made you expect one of them next. The finger exercises are not among the listed achievements, and the sentence ranks them above everything listed.

B.why: You assumed that a long list of successes leads to a conclusion. Her violins and treatise do not explain why she valued the exercises most, so 'Thus' invents a cause.

C.why: This is the list trap. 'Indeed' intensifies the previous point, as if the next sentence named an even grander success. The sentence instead calls her favourite achievement 'modest' and ranks it above the impressive list, so it turns against the list.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Seismologists once assumed that, during any earthquake, the buildings nearest the epicenter would always shake hardest. ______ in 1985, an earthquake centered roughly 350 kilometers from Mexico City toppled hundreds of buildings there while towns far closer to the epicenter suffered less, because the city rests on soft lakebed sediments that amplified the seismic waves.
explanation: The first sentence states an old assumption. The second gives a real event that disproves it: distant buildings fell while nearer towns did better. When a mistaken belief is followed by what actually happened, 'In reality' is the correction word.

B.why: You saw a single dated event and treated it as an illustration. An example has to support the claim before it, and this event is a counterexample that disproves the assumption.

C.why: You noticed the 'because' and the cause-and-effect language about sediments and carried it back to the blank. The seismologists' assumption did not lead to the 1985 damage. The damage contradicts the assumption.

D.why: Both sentences are about how hard buildings shake, so you read them as moving in the same direction. 'Likewise' would need the second sentence to support the assumption, but it overturns it.
